data.hypothesis: The catalog contains five distinct valid OpenMP programs; the flattened static-row parent measured 0.2292 s versus the 0.4575 s serial baseline, while explicit row-block and plane-group variants were slower in aggregate. This experiment tests whether assigning static contiguous tiles of 16 rows reduces per-row y/z index reconstruction while retaining serial fallback, per-timestep regions at a one-thread budget, and a persistent team for larger budgets. The measurements must determine whether that arithmetic reduction outweighs tile-loop overhead at the official one- and four-core settings.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as a reason to test a contrasting scheduling granularity, not as proof that row mapping caused the timing difference.
memory_lessons.claim: The explicit row-block candidate measured 0.2615 s and the flattened static-row parent measured 0.2292 s; both were correct, but the aggregate results do not isolate the cause or the one- versus four-thread behavior.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure static contiguous row tiles against the flattened row loop at the official thread settings, including full boundary and output checks.

data.notes: This is a single row-granularity experiment; it keeps the six-step arithmetic, ping-pong buffers, initialization, serial cutoff, and call-local OpenMP thread limits. The tile traversal covers each active y/z row exactly once, including tiles crossing a plane boundary. No commands were run and correctness or performance was not independently verified here; the controller should run the full small-case and n=256 checks and official one- and four-core measurements.
transformations: Preserved the serial stencil implementation, output initialization, six-step parity, and low-work serial fallback.
Changed flattened row work to static tiles of 16 contiguous rows; each tile reconstructs its initial y/z position once and advances across any plane boundary.
Kept a parallel region per timestep for one-thread calls and one persistent OpenMP region across timesteps for larger budgets, using num_threads from the call and no global OpenMP state.
